title: What would happen if you stood on Venus?

lines.text: If you stepped out of a spaceship onto the surface of Venus, how long could your body survive?
lines.caps: How long could you *survive | on the surface of *Venus?

lines.text: The terrifying answer is less than one single second.
lines.caps: The terrifying answer is *less | than one *second!

lines.text: Venus is trapped under a runaway greenhouse effect of ninety-six percent carbon dioxide.
lines.caps: Trapped under a runaway *greenhouse | effect of carbon *dioxide

lines.text: Surface temperatures reach a blistering nine hundred degrees Fahrenheit, hot enough to melt solid lead.
lines.caps: Temperatures reach *900 degrees | hot enough to melt *lead!

lines.text: The atmospheric pressure is ninety times heavier than Earth's, equivalent to being three thousand feet underwater.
lines.caps: Atmospheric pressure is equal to *3,000 feet | deep in the *ocean

lines.text: Your skull and ribcage would be crushed flat like an aluminum soda can instantly.
lines.caps: Your body would be *crushed flat | like an empty soda *can

lines.text: Thick clouds above rain corrosive sulfuric acid that evaporates before touching the scorched basalt ground.
lines.caps: Clouds rain corrosive *sulfuric acid | over volcanic *rock!

lines.text: Venus is the absolute closest thing to a literal hell in our solar system.
lines.caps: Venus is a literal *hell | inside our solar *system!
